name: dggs-biodiversity-bias — a common DGGS for the integration of biodiversity with Copernicus EO and Destination Earth climate models
description: A pedagogical and supporting-evidence repository for the EGU 2026 talk EGU26-11348 (Fouilloux et al., LifeWatch ERIC, ESSI2.6). Eight reproducible notebooks make a four-step layered argument: (1) Equal-area is necessary for biodiversity counts — lat-lon over-counts toward the equator by up to 23x at 5-degree resolution, purely from cell geometry. (2) Six equal-area choices pass the count test on real GBIF data: HEALPix, H3, rHEALPix, ISEA3H, Mollweide, and the EEA reference grid (LAEA Europe / EPSG:3035 / INSPIRE / Habitats Directive standard) all agree on biodiversity density patterns over Quercus suber's Mediterranean range — for biodiversity counts in isolation, the choice between equal-area DGGS is not a count-correctness question. (3) The DGGS family (HEALPix, H3, rHEALPix, ISEA3H) preserves cell shape across latitudes while the projection family (Behrmann, Mollweide, EEA reference grid) does not — a property that matters for ML kernels on stacked feature cubes. (4) HEALPix is the right common DGGS for the integrated future of biodiversity science with high-resolution Copernicus EO and Destination Earth climate models, by virtue of its native geometric-deep-learning ecosystem (DeepSphere, foscat / FIESTA scattering networks), native sphere-harmonic transforms, NESTED bit-shift O(1) hierarchical refinement, iso-latitude pixelization, and a credible ellipsoidally-correct path via rHEALPix or 'Ellipsoidal HEALPix' (the ESA GRID4EARTH approach). The repository is the biodiversity-side version of the case GRID4EARTH makes for Ellipsoidal HEALPix as a Common DGGS bridging Copernicus EO and Destination Earth.
